newsitem.title: FRANCE: French telephone numbers to gain two new digits.
newsitem.headline: French telephone numbers to gain two new digits.

text.p: French telephone numbers will grow to 10 digits from the current eight digits at 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) on Friday, state-owned France Telecom announced.
The company has mounted a massive public relations campaign to prepare people for the change, which is intended to keep France in step with international telephone standards.
It said the new system, which affects both international and domestic dialing, would allow France to have 470 million different numbers, enough to last until 2050.

All domestic calls will gain a two-digit prefix beginning with a zero. For calls from outside the country, the prefix will be 33 -- France's current international access code -- plus the second digit of the new prefix without an initial zero.
Thus, domestic calls to the Paris region will add the prefix 01. For those placed from abroad, the number will remain unchanged, beginning with the access code 33 followed by 1.

Domestic calls to northwestern France, including the cities Brest and Le Havre, add the prefix 02 and international calls will begin with the digits 33 2. The northeast, including Reims, Strasbourg and Nancy, gain the prefix 03 (or 33 3 from abroad).

Domestic calls to southeastern France, including Marseilles, Lyon and Nice, will be preceded by 04 (or 33 4 from abroad), while calls to the southwest, including Bordeaux and Toulouse, will gain the prefix 05 (33 5 from outside the country).
Mobile telephone numbers, regardless of the owner's address, will gain the prefix 06 (or 33 6 from abroad).
